source.original_text: For any probability measure mu on any measurable carrier and any a.e.-strongly-measurable real f with a finite uniform a.e. bound and zero mean, all sufficiently small real parameters e give an affine density 1+e*f bounded below by one half almost everywhere. The literal measure mu.withDensity(ofReal(1+e*f)) is a probability measure, and its canonical extended-real KL relative to mu equals ofReal of the real integral of q(1+e*f), where q(u)=u*log(u)-u+1. Thus KL itself is finite. This is a measure-theoretic prerequisite of a source perturbation expansion, not that full limit, LSI, Fisher or Poincare.

lean.statement: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace X] (mu : Measure X) [IsProbabilityMeasure mu] (f : X → ℝ), AEStronglyMeasurable f mu → ∀ {M : ℝ}, (∀ᵐ x ∂mu, |f x| ≤ M) → (∫ x, f x ∂mu) = 0 → ∀ᶠ e : ℝ in 𝓝 (0 : ℝ), (∀ᵐ x ∂mu, (1 : ℝ) / 2 ≤ 1 + e * f x) ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure (mu.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (1 + e * f x))) ∧ InformationTheory.klDiv (mu.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (1 + e * f x))) mu = ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x, InformationTheory.klFun (1 + e * f x) ∂mu)

blind_reconstruction.text: For every measurable space X, every probability measure mu on X, every function f : X -> R that is mu-almost everywhere equal to a strongly measurable function, and every real number M, assume that |f(x)| <= M for mu-almost every x and that the real Bochner integral of f with respect to mu equals 0. Then there exists a real delta > 0 such that, for every real e with |e| < delta, all three statements hold simultaneously: (1) 1/2 <= 1 + e*f(x) for mu-almost every x; (2) the measure nu_e = mu.withDensity(x |-> ENNReal.ofReal(1 + e*f(x))) is a probability measure; and (3) the canonical nonnegative extended-real divergence klDiv(nu_e, mu) equals ENNReal.ofReal of the real Bochner integral of (1 + e*f(x))*Real.log(1 + e*f(x)) + 1 - (1 + e*f(x)) with respect to mu. Here ENNReal.ofReal(r) is max(r, 0) embedded in the nonnegative extended reals; Real.log and the real Bochner integral use their totalized definitions. The quantifier over e includes e = 0 and both signs of sufficiently small e. All almost-everywhere assertions are with respect to mu.

import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Group.Bounded
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum

/-!
# Actual bounded centered perturbation laws

For sufficiently small real `e`, the literal density `1 + e * f` is positive
and has mass one. Its canonical KL divergence is finite and equals its
compensated entropy integral. Measurability, normalization, Radon--Nikodym
identification and entropy integrability are proved, not public premises.

This supplies a measure-theoretic step in Chewi, *Log-Concave Sampling*
(August 20, 2026), Exercise 1.7 / (1.E.1), also used by Corollary 2.1.2.
It does not prove the full exercise, Fisher limit, LSI-domain extension or PI.
-/

open MeasureTheory Filter
open scoped Topology

noncomputable section

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.InformationTheory.BoundedPerturbationLaw

/-- Bounded centered perturbations define actual probability laws near zero.
Their canonical extended-real KL, not just its totalized real value, is the
finite compensated entropy integral. The lower bound includes `e = 0`. -/
theorem eventually_isProbabilityMeasure_and_klDiv_eq_one_add_mul
    {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] (mu : Measure X) [IsProbabilityMeasure mu]
    (f : X → ℝ) (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f mu) {M : ℝ}
    (hbound : ∀ᵐ x ∂mu, |f x| ≤ M) (hcenter : (∫ x, f x ∂mu) = 0) :
    ∀ᶠ e : ℝ in 𝓝 (0 : ℝ),
      (∀ᵐ x ∂mu, (1 : ℝ) / 2 ≤ 1 + e * f x) ∧
      IsProbabilityMeasure (mu.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (1 + e * f x))) ∧
      _root_.InformationTheory.klDiv
        (mu.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (1 + e * f x))) mu =
        ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x, _root_.InformationTheory.klFun (1 + e * f x) ∂mu) := by
  have hfi : Integrable f mu := (integrable_const |M|).mono' hf (by
    filter_upwards [hbound] with x hx
    simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs] using hx.trans (le_abs_self M))
  have hsmall : ∀ᶠ e : ℝ in 𝓝 (0 : ℝ), |e| * |M| < 1 / 2 :=
    (isOpen_lt (continuous_abs.mul continuous_const) continuous_const).mem_nhds (by norm_num)
  filter_upwards [hsmall] with e he
  let p : X → ℝ := fun x => 1 + e * f x
  let nu := mu.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (p x))
  have hp : AEStronglyMeasurable p mu := aestronglyMeasurable_const.add (hf.const_mul e)
  have hpI : Integrable p mu := (integrable_const 1).add (hfi.const_mul e)
  have hinterval : ∀ᵐ x ∂mu, p x ∈ Set.Icc ((1 : ℝ) / 2) (3 / 2) := by
    filter_upwards [hbound] with x hx
    have hprod : |e * f x| < 1 / 2 := by
      rw [abs_mul]
      exact (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hx.trans (le_abs_self M)) (abs_nonneg e)).trans_lt he
    obtain ⟨hlo, hhi⟩ := abs_lt.mp hprod
    constructor <;> dsimp [p] <;> linarith
  have hpos : ∀ᵐ x ∂mu, 0 ≤ p x := hinterval.mono fun _ hx => by linarith [hx.1]
  have hmass : (∫ x, p x ∂mu) = 1 := by
    rw [integral_add (integrable_const 1) (hfi.const_mul e), integral_const_mul, hcenter]
    simp
  have hprob : IsProbabilityMeasure nu := by
    constructor
    change mu.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (p x)) Set.univ = 1
    rw [withDensity_apply _ MeasurableSet.univ, Measure.restrict_univ,
      ← ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal hpI hpos, hmass]
    norm_num
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure nu := hprob
  have hrn : (fun x => (nu.rnDeriv mu x).toReal) =ᵐ[mu] p := by
    filter_upwards [Measure.rnDeriv_withDensity₀ mu hp.aemeasurable.ennreal_ofReal, hpos]
      with x hx hxpos
    exact (congrArg ENNReal.toReal hx).trans (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal hxpos)
  obtain ⟨B, hB⟩ := (isCompact_Icc : IsCompact (Set.Icc ((1 : ℝ) / 2) (3 / 2))).exists_bound_of_continuousOn
    _root_.InformationTheory.continuous_klFun.continuousOn
  have hq : Integrable (fun x => _root_.InformationTheory.klFun (p x)) mu :=
    (integrable_const B).mono'
      (_root_.InformationTheory.continuous_klFun.comp_aestronglyMeasurable hp)
      (hinterval.mono fun x hx => hB (p x) hx)
  have hqRN : Integrable (fun x => _root_.InformationTheory.klFun (nu.rnDeriv mu x).toReal) mu :=
    hq.congr (hrn.mono fun x hx => congrArg _root_.InformationTheory.klFun hx.symm)
  have hac : nu ≪ mu := withDensity_absolutelyContinuous mu _
  have hllr := (_root_.InformationTheory.integrable_klFun_rnDeriv_iff hac).mp hqRN
  refine ⟨hinterval.mono fun _ hx => hx.1, hprob, ?_⟩
  rw [_root_.InformationTheory.klDiv_eq_integral_klFun, if_pos ⟨hac, hllr⟩]
  congr 1
  exact integral_congr_ae (hrn.mono fun x hx => congrArg _root_.InformationTheory.klFun hx)

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.InformationTheory.BoundedPerturbationLaw

candidate_publication_context.statement: The linearization route uses the actual measure with density 1+epsilon*f relative to the reference probability law. For a bounded centered measurable real test, sufficiently small real epsilon makes this density at least one half almost everywhere, defines a probability law, and gives finite canonical KL equal to the compensated entropy integral. This item isolates that supporting construction; the source KL asymptotic and final Poincare conclusion are not asserted by it.
assumptions: The reference law is a probability measure, and the real test is bounded and centered. Smooth compact tests in the literal hint are special cases.
Corollary2.1.2 uses bounded smooth centered tests with compact gradient support, not necessarily compact support of the function.

This generic supporting theorem needs only a.e. strong measurability and an a.e. finite uniform bound. It proves positivity, mass one, RN identification, entropy integrability and canonical KL finiteness rather than assuming them.

obligations.label: Small-parameter positivity, actual unit-mass law, RN representative and finite canonical KL formula
Compose with the separate actual compensated integral limit
Actual Fisher limit, LSI admissibility and final PI/core domain

lesson.title: A real perturbation law with finite canonical KL
lesson.classification: shared measure-theoretic construction for Exercise 1.7; not the complete exercise
lesson.statement: Let mu be a probability measure on any measurable space. Suppose f is real-valued, a.e. strongly measurable, uniformly a.e. bounded by a finite real M, and has mean zero. For all sufficiently small real epsilon, the affine density is at least one half almost everywhere, its literal nonnegative-density construction is a probability law, and its canonical extended-real KL equals the real compensated entropy integral embedded in the nonnegative extended reals. In particular the divergence is genuinely finite, not merely assigned a totalized real value.
assumptions: mu is a probability law on an arbitrary measurable carrier. No smooth Gibbs density or Euclidean geometry is required.

f is a.e. strongly measurable, |f| <= M almost everywhere, and its actual integral is zero. Its integrability is derived from the essential bound and finite measure. No pointwise representative, smoothness or compact support is assumed.

The neighborhood is an ordinary two-sided real neighborhood of zero and includes epsilon=0. No division by M or epsilon is used. Positivity, mass one, the RN representative and finite KL are conclusions, not supplied certificates.

steps.title: Choose a neighborhood that also handles the zero bound
steps.text: At epsilon=0 the product of the absolute values is zero, so continuity gives a neighborhood where it is less than one half. Combine this with the a.e. bound on f. The resulting closed interval contains every relevant density value; in particular the clipping in ofReal has no effect almost everywhere.
steps.lean: isOpen_lt and continuous_abs produce hsmall. The a.e. interval hinterval is obtained from abs_mul and abs_lt, not assumed.

steps.title: Prove the actual density has unit mass
steps.text: The finite probability measure and essential bound make f integrable, hence also the affine density. Now use linearity of the actual Bochner integral and the zero mean. Converting this nonnegative integral into a lintegral proves the literal withDensity measure is a probability measure.
steps.lean: Integrable.mono' derives hfi; integral_add and integral_const_mul give hmass. withDensity_apply and ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal construct hprob.

steps.title: Identify the Radon–Nikodym representative almost everywhere
steps.text: The law is absolutely continuous because it was constructed by withDensity. Its RN derivative equals the supplied nonnegative density almost everywhere. The previously proved nonnegativity then identifies the real-valued RN representative with the affine expression. This is an a.e. statement, not pointwise equality or a differentiability claim.
steps.lean: Measure.rnDeriv_withDensity₀ uses a.e. measurability; ENNReal.toReal_ofReal uses hpos. No canonical pointwise representative is invented.

steps.title: Produce entropy integrability on a fixed compact interval
steps.text: The compensated entropy function is continuous, including at zero. On the compact interval from the first step its norm has a finite bound. Since mu is finite, that constant is integrable. Composition preserves a.e. strong measurability, so domination proves the actual entropy integrand integrable.
steps.lean: IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn supplies a finite bound; continuous_klFun.comp_aestronglyMeasurable and Integrable.mono' derive hq. No entropy integrability binder is added.

steps.title: Identify finite KL itself, not only its real projection
steps.text: Transfer entropy integrability across the a.e. RN identity. The canonical equivalence gives integrability of the log likelihood ratio under the perturbed law. Apply Mathlib's formula for the extended-real divergence, then substitute the actual density. Its value is ofReal of a real integral, which cannot be infinity. A toReal identity alone would not establish this.
steps.lean: integrable_klFun_rnDeriv_iff and klDiv_eq_integral_klFun close the integrability branch; integral_congr_ae substitutes hrn. The focused test derives finiteness using ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top.

steps.title: Connect to the analytic parent without claiming the exercise
steps.text: This law identity is the measure-theoretic input to the already compiled compensated integral limit. A focused test actually composes the two results to obtain the real-valued canonical KL asymptotic, using nonnegativity before taking toReal. That example is not a separately published canonical theorem or Bench question. The source's Fisher limit, LSI admissibility and PI domain extension remain independent. Centering does not make a function compactly supported.
steps.lean: The owning module constructs the finite law/KL interface. Tests/Shared/BoundedPerturbationLaw.lean combines it with tendsto_integral_klFun_one_add_mul_div_sq using eventual equality and Tendsto.congr'; the example earns no extra public leaf.

lesson.lean_statement: The eventual conjunction records the density lower bound, actual probability-measure instance and exact ENNReal KL formula. The theorem uses no new project definition or hypothetical law witness.
lesson.lean_proof: A small-parameter interval gives integrability, mass one and an actual withDensity probability law; the canonical RN identity and compact entropy bound then select the finite branch of canonical KL. All intermediate facts are constructed inside one public theorem.
